artifacts.summary: Research on the detail-free blocking issue-log entry at orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh's partial) arm: the described raw jq join() root cause was already superseded incidentally by an unrelated task (commit 83898819a), but the fix omits verbatim_goal, still swallows jq errors via 2>/dev/null, and test fixture 830 never asserts issues.jsonl content. Settles classification: keep severity=blocking (meets the admission test exactly), replace --class "environment" with a new open-enum class value (no issue-log.md edit required), add identity-keyed de-duplication for repeated partial dispatches, and drop the suppress-on-user_decision idea (no mechanical "answered" test exists, and issues.jsonl never surfaces mid-run so there is no user-visible duplicate to suppress).

memory_candidates.content: In a concurrent-batch orchestration run, an unrelated task's uncommitted edit to a shared file can be swept into a different task's commit (git-commit-scoped.sh stages/commits whatever is on disk at commit time, not just the invoking task's own changes). Confirmed instance: orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh's partial_blockers_detail jq rendering fix landed inside commit 83898819a ("task 304: orchestration paused (cycle 3)"), attributed by that task's own summary to a sibling task in a declared file_scope overlap set. When auditing "when did X get fixed" on a frequently-touched shared script, check git log -S on the exact changed substring rather than trusting the owning task's own narrative -- the commit that introduced a fix is not necessarily the task whose summary you'd expect to describe it.

issue-log.md's --class field is a documented open enum: issue-record.sh accepts any value outside its 16-class seed table with only a stderr warning, never a refusal, and promoting a recurring new value into the documented seed table is explicitly "a documentation change ... never an enforcement change in the writer." This means a call site with a wrong hard-coded --class default can be fixed by substituting a new, honest literal with zero edits to issue-log.md itself -- useful when a sibling/concurrent record has claimed the format document as its own file territory and a format-document edit would otherwise require a serializing dependency edge.
